metrics.label: Yards per play
metrics.dfn: Yards gained per offensive snap: runs, passes and sacks. Interception plays count as 0 yards (return yards belong to the defense).

metrics.label: Points per drive
metrics.dfn: Points the offense scores per possession (TD = 7, FG = 3; defensive and return scores don't count). Every drive counts, including ones that end a half.

metrics.label: Moves the chains before 3rd down
metrics.dfn: Share of 1st downs that become a new 1st down or a touchdown on 1st or 2nd down, without facing 3rd down. Drives with a kneel-down are left out.

metrics.label: Yards per carry
metrics.dfn: Yards per designed run or scramble. Sacks don't count as runs here (college box scores count them), so a team that can't protect its quarterback doesn't look like a team that can't run. Kneel-downs are left out.

metrics.label: Yards per dropback
metrics.dfn: Passing yards per dropback, with sacks counted as the yards they lose and interceptions as 0. A dropback is a pass (complete, incomplete or intercepted) or a sack; scrambles count as runs. Spikes are left out.

metrics.label: Sack rate
metrics.dfn: Sacks per dropback (passes, interceptions and sacks; scrambles count as runs). Strip-sacks count. Offense: how often its QB goes down (lower is better). Defense: how often it gets there (higher is better).

metrics.label: Explosive plays
metrics.dfn: Runs and completions of 20+ yards, as a share of offensive snaps. Return yards don't count.

metrics.label: TDs on trips inside the 40
metrics.dfn: Drives with at least one snap at the opponent's 40 or closer that end in a touchdown, as a share of those drives. A long touchdown from farther out isn't a trip.
ph: finishing trips inside the 40 with touchdowns
keeping trips inside its 40 out of the end zone

metrics.label: Points per trip inside the 40
metrics.dfn: Points per drive with at least one snap at the opponent's 40 or closer (TD = 7, FG = 3, nothing = 0).
ph: limiting points on trips inside its 40

metrics.label: 3rd-down conversion rate
metrics.dfn: 3rd-down snaps that gain the yards needed or score. Snaps wiped out by a penalty aren't counted at all, and a turnover is never a conversion.

metrics.label: Average distance on 3rd down
metrics.dfn: How many yards to go on an average 3rd down. Offense: shorter is easier. Defense: longer means it put offenses behind the chains.

metrics.label: Red zone TD rate
metrics.dfn: Drives that reach the opponent's 20 or closer and end in a touchdown. Smaller samples than trips inside the 40.

metrics.label: Average starting field position
metrics.dfn: Average yard line where drives begin (own 25 = 25). Comes from defense, special teams and turnovers together.
ph: starting drives in good field position

metrics.label: Turnovers per game
metrics.dfn: Interceptions and lost fumbles per game, as counted in DAWG's game records. ESPN's box score can differ by one in a game (it also counts special-teams fumbles). Turnover rates swing a lot; much of it is luck.

questions: Can they run it, and can they throw it?
Can they get off the field?
